en.title: Set up a Hong Kong company as a non-Hong Kong resident – Is it possible?

blocks.text: ✅Yes — and you don’t need to fly to Hong Kong to incorporate.✈️
Myth: “I must be there in person.”

Fact: Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Hong Kong private companies have no nationality, residency, visa or local-partner requirement for directors or shareholders. A private company needs at least one natural-person director, but that director can be a non-resident. You can be the sole director and 100% shareholder from anywhere.
What must stay in Hong Kong:
✅ Company secretary — an HK resident, or a TCSP-licensed corporate secretary. If you are the sole director, you cannot also act as company secretary.
✅ Registered office — a physical HK address; PO box not accepted.
✅ Designated representative — for the Significant Controllers Register.
What you don’t need:
❌ HK visa or travel for incorporation
❌ Local director/shareholder
❌ Minimum paid-up capital — but at least one share must be issued
The incorporation process can be completed remotely. Bank account opening is separate: most banks require director/beneficial owner KYC, by video call or in person, depending on the bank.
